The curvature $κ(t)$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}.
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$, ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}),$ and $‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({sin}^{2}⁡t-{cos}^{2}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =⟨2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4}),\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi }{4}⟩=⟨2,\sqrt{2}⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖ & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(\sqrt{2})^{2}}=\sqrt{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find ${r}^{″}(t)$ and ${r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨4\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =⟨4\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4}),\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{4}⟩=⟨0,\,-\sqrt{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})$ and ${r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4})$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})\times {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =⟨2,\,\sqrt{2},0⟩\times ⟨0,\,-\sqrt{2},\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & \sqrt{2} & 0 \\ 0 & -\sqrt{2} & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}2 & \sqrt{2} \\ 0 & -\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =-2\sqrt{2}\,k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})\times {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖ & =2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the curvature at $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})\times {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖}{{‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖}^{3}}=\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{(\sqrt{6})^{3}}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

The curvature κ(t) is given by

κ(t)=‖r′(t)×r″(t)‖‖r′(t)‖3.

First, we calculate r′(t), r′(π4), and ‖r′(π4)‖:

r′(t)=⟨ddt(sin2⁡t−cos2⁡t),ddt(2sin⁡t)⟩=⟨2sin⁡tcos⁡t+2cos⁡tsin⁡t,2cos⁡t⟩=⟨2sin⁡2t,2cos⁡t⟩r′(π4)=⟨2sin⁡(2⋅π4),2cos⁡π4⟩=⟨2,2⟩‖r′(π4)‖=22+(2)2=6

Now, we find r″(t) and r″(π4):

r″(t)=⟨ddt(2sin⁡2t),ddt(2cos⁡t)⟩=⟨4cos⁡2t,−2sin⁡t⟩r″(π4)=⟨4cos⁡(2⋅π4),−2sin⁡π4⟩=⟨0,−2⟩

Next, we compute the cross product by considering r′(π4) and r″(π4) as 3-dimensional vectors with zero z-components:

r′(π4)×r″(π4)=⟨2,2,0⟩×⟨0,−2,0⟩=ijk2200−20=220−2k=−22k‖r′(π4)×r″(π4)‖=22

Therefore, the curvature at t=π4 is

κ(π4)=‖r′(π4)×r″(π4)‖‖r′(π4)‖3=22(6)3=39.
